source_text: Ἔδοξα δέ ποτε τὸ μέγιστον τῶν ἀγαθῶν βρῶσιν εἶναι καὶ πόσιν· κἀκεῖνον θεοφιλέστατον, ὃς ἂν τούτων ἀπολαύῃ παρὰ τὸν βίον, ὡς οἷόν τε μάλιστα· καὶ παραμυθίαν τῆς ζωῆς, τὴν τοιαύτην εὐθυμίαν μόνην ἡγησάμην· καὶ τοίνυν προσεῖχον οὐδενὶ ἑτέρῳ, ἢ τῇ οἰήσει ταύτῃ, ὡς μήτε νύκτωρ μήτε μεθημέραν ἁπάντων, ὅσα πρὸς τρυφὴν ἀνθρώποις εὕρηται, ἐμαυτὸν ἀπάγειν. Ἔγνων τε τοσοῦτον, ὅτι ἐν ἐκείνοις τὶς ἐμφύρων, οὐδαμῶς δυνήσεται, οὐδὲ πολλὰ μοχθήσας, εὑρεῖν τὸ ὄντως ἀγαθόν.
thought_title: Testing pleasure as the greatest good
orientation: Solomon (reported by Gregory) recounts his experiment of devoting himself entirely to eating, drinking, and cheerfulness as the supposed highest good, only to discover that this path cannot lead to the true good.
pass_a_gloss: It seemed to me once that the greatest of goods is eating and drinking; and that man is most God-beloved who enjoys these things beyond his lifetime, as it is most possible; and I considered such cheerfulness to be the only consolation of life; and therefore I applied myself to nothing else except this notion, so that I might lead myself away neither by night nor by day from all things found for human luxury; I came to know, however, that anyone indulging in these things will by no means be able to find the truly good, even after toiling much.

lemmas.gloss: it seemed to me / I thought
most God-beloved / most loved by God

choices.why: Glossary does not cover this superlative; literal 'God-beloved' matches the theological weight and avoids 'dear to God' which weakens the force.
In context of pleasure-seeking 'alongside/beyond life' means exceeding the normal span; 'beyond his lifetime' captures the sense of stretching indulgence past life's limit.
Plain English for the inward state Solomon treats as life's only consolation; 'good spirits' is too colloquial.
Refers to the fixed practice of pleasure; 'opinion' or 'supposition' would miss the behavioral sense of 'devoting oneself'.
Active present participle: the subject inflames himself in these pleasures; 'indulging' keeps the self-involvement.

bible_refs.note: βρῶσιν εἶναι καὶ πόσιν / εὐθυμίαν / προσεῖχον … ἐμαυτὸν ἀπάγειν

pass_b_english: I once thought the greatest good was eating and drinking, and that the person most God-beloved was the one who enjoys these things throughout his life as much as possible. I considered cheerfulness of this sort the only consolation of life. So I gave my attention to nothing else but this notion, so that neither by night nor by day did I hold myself back from any of the pleasures people have devised. I came to know that no one indulging in these things will ever be able to find the true good, no matter how much he toils.

problems.why: παρὰ τὸν βίον means 'throughout/during life'. 'Beyond his lifetime' implies an afterlife and reverses the sense.
problems.fix: the one who enjoys these things throughout his life as much as possible

problems.quote: so as to drag myself toward every pleasure known to human beings, neither by night nor by day
problems.source_quote: ὡς μήτε νύκτωρ μήτε μεθημέραν ἁπάντων, ὅσα πρὸς τρυφὴν ἀνθρώποις εὕρηται, ἐμαυτὸν ἀπάγειν
problems.why: ἀπάγειν means to withdraw or hold back. The source says he never held himself back from any pleasure, night or day. English reverses this and garbles the negation.
problems.fix: so that neither by night nor by day did I hold myself back from any of the pleasures people have devised.

edits.old: beyond his lifetime as much as possible
edits.new: throughout his life as much as possible

edits.old: So I devoted myself to nothing else but this habit, so as to drag myself toward every pleasure known to human beings, neither by night nor by day.
edits.new: So I devoted myself to nothing else but this habit, so that neither by night nor by day did I hold myself back from any of the pleasures people have devised.

fixed: Changed 'beyond his lifetime' to 'throughout his life' to match παρὰ τὸν βίον (during/throughout life).
Corrected the reversal of ἀπάγειν (hold back/withdraw): the Greek says he never held himself back from any pleasure, night or day.

problems.quote: So I devoted myself to nothing else but this habit
problems.source_quote: προσεῖχον οὐδενὶ ἑτέρῳ, ἢ τῇ οἰήσει ταύτῃ
problems.why: οἴησις means opinion or conviction, not habit. The sentence says he was devoted to this belief, which is the notion he held about the greatest good.
problems.fix: So I gave my attention to nothing else but this notion, so that neither by night nor by day did I hold myself back from any of the pleasures people have devised.

edits.old: So I devoted myself to nothing else but this habit
edits.new: So I gave my attention to nothing else but this notion
